I'll think this through as the farmer and then write out my plan.

**My thinking:**

I've been farming this 8 mu for many years. Cotton is my main crop — around here everyone grows cotton, the gin station buys it, and I know how to handle it. Last year I put about 5 mu in cotton, 2 mu in maize for our own eating and for feed, and 1 mu in mungbean because mungbean doesn't need much and my husband likes to sell a little at the market. I'll do the same this year — why change when it worked?

For cotton, I buy Bt cotton seed from the dealer in town — the improved kind, everyone uses it now because the bollworm used to eat us alive before. I put on two bags of compound fertilizer (diammonium) before planting, that's about 50 jin per mu, and then I topdress with urea when the cotton starts flowering, maybe another bag across the field. That comes to roughly 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 8 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium. Cotton here needs spraying many times — bollworm, aphid, spider mite — I spray maybe 6 or 7 times through the season, can't avoid it. I water from the well 3 times if the rain is poor: once after planting, once at flowering, once at bolling. I plough before planting, that's how my husband always does it.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed, summer maize after wheat-free fallow. I put one bag compound under the row and topdress urea at knee-high. About 15 kg N, 5 kg P, 5 kg K per mu. Two sprays — one for armyworm, one for borer. Irrigate twice. Rotary till is enough for maize, saves diesel.

For mungbean, I use the seed I saved from last year, traditional kind. Mungbean makes its own fertilizer from the roots, I don't put much — just a little compound, maybe 3 kg N, 3 kg P, 2 kg K. One spray if aphids come, one watering. Rotary till.

I expect cotton around 250 kg seed cotton per mu if weather is alright, maize around 500 kg, mungbean around 120 kg. Last year was similar.
